subject.title: fix(release): keep conflicting npm lock forks pinned

question: Should release packaging adopt the newest locked stable patch as the canonical npm override when distinct pnpm peer contexts collapse to one npm parent selector?
rationale: The related merged change established parent-scoped overrides as the normal policy, while this PR introduces a deliberate exception needed for npm’s less expressive selector model; choosing that release contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Accept the narrow collision fallback
options.body: Adopt the deterministic global newest-patch pin only for same-parent peer-context collisions with locked stable versions on one major/minor line, while preserving scoped forks otherwise.

options.title: Keep all forks scoped
options.body: Retain the prior policy and treat the Discord packaging path as requiring a different npm-lock representation or packaging approach.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow collision fallback
recommendation.body: Adopt the deterministic global newest-patch pin only for same-parent peer-context collisions with locked stable versions on one major/minor line, while preserving scoped forks otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged history shows steipete established the preceding override policy and documented its release rationale.
